perf.summary: Fuse the div/mod pair so the divisor is read once and the quotient computed once.
perf.currentCost: Per loop iteration: one load of setSizes[i], plus a separate '%' and '/' on the same operands. Even with CSE most JITs/Burst will emit one IDIV and derive the remainder, but writing them separately can leave a redundant load and risks two divides if the loads are not proven identical.
perf.proposedChange: int s = setSizes[i]; int q = index / s; dst[i] = index - q * s; index = q;  (one load, one divide, remainder via mul/sub).
perf.rationale: IDIV is ~20-40 cycles and is the loop bottleneck; computing remainder as index - q*s replaces a second potential divide with a cheap IMUL+SUB and guarantees the divisor load is hoisted into a register once.
perf.risk: Semantics identical for non-negative index and positive setSizes (the only valid inputs for an index into a Cartesian product). For negative index the truncated-division identity index = q*s + r still holds in C#, so no signed edge case is introduced.

perf.summary: Return type int silently overflows; document or widen to long to match the index space used by GetAt.
perf.currentCost: total is int; product of setSizes overflows past 2^31 with no signal, yet GetAt walks an index that could exceed int range only if count exceeds int.
perf.proposedChange: Either keep int (consistent with GetAt's int index) and add a named-constant comment that caller guarantees product < int.MaxValue, or provide a long-returning ComputeCountInt64 overload for large product spaces. No code-path change required if int is the intended contract.
perf.rationale: Consistency of the index width across ComputeCount and GetAt avoids silent truncation bugs; this is an API clarity issue, not a cycle cost.
perf.risk: Pure documentation/overload addition; does not alter existing behavior.
